subject: Calculus and its Applications
title: Multiple Integrals — One-Mark MCQ Practice
note: Original ACADRIX practice MCQs for R-2025 preparation. These are not official university questions or PYQs.

questions.q: A double integral over a region R is commonly written as
questions.explanation: A double integral accumulates a function over a two-dimensional region using an area element dA.

questions.q: In Cartesian coordinates, the area element for a double integral is
questions.explanation: For Cartesian coordinates, dA = dx dy (or dy dx).

questions.q: The order of integration in ∫∫ f(x,y) dy dx is
questions.explanation: The differential nearest the function is integrated first, so dy indicates integration with respect to y first.

questions.q: Changing the order of integration is mainly useful when
options: the new order makes evaluation easier
questions.answer: the new order makes evaluation easier
questions.explanation: Changing order can simplify limits or make one of the integrations elementary.

questions.q: For polar coordinates, x is represented by
questions.explanation: The Cartesian-polar relation is x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ.

questions.q: For polar coordinates, y is represented by
questions.explanation: The standard transformation is y = r sin θ.

questions.q: The Jacobian factor for converting dx dy to polar coordinates is
questions.explanation: The polar area element is dA = r dr dθ.

questions.q: The polar form of x² + y² is
questions.explanation: Since x² + y² = r², circular regions become simpler in polar coordinates.

questions.q: The region x² + y² ≤ a² represents a
questions.explanation: The inequality describes a disk centered at the origin with radius a.

questions.q: In polar coordinates, a disk of radius a centered at the origin has radial limits
questions.explanation: Every point inside the disk has radial distance between 0 and a.

questions.q: The volume element in Cartesian coordinates for a triple integral is
questions.explanation: A three-dimensional Cartesian volume element is dV = dx dy dz.

questions.q: A triple integral is primarily used to integrate over a
questions.explanation: Triple integrals accumulate quantities throughout a three-dimensional region.

questions.q: In cylindrical coordinates, the Cartesian variables x and y are related to r and θ by
questions.explanation: Cylindrical coordinates extend polar coordinates into three dimensions while retaining z.

questions.q: The cylindrical-coordinate volume element is
questions.explanation: The Jacobian for cylindrical coordinates contributes the factor r.

questions.q: In spherical coordinates, the radial distance from the origin is denoted by
questions.explanation: Spherical coordinates commonly use ρ for radial distance, together with angular coordinates.

questions.q: For spherical coordinates, x can be expressed as
questions.explanation: With φ measured from the positive z-axis, x = ρ sinφ cosθ.

questions.q: The spherical-coordinate volume element is
questions.explanation: The spherical Jacobian is ρ² sinφ.

questions.q: A sphere centered at the origin is especially convenient to describe using
questions.explanation: A sphere is described simply by a constant radial limit ρ = a.

questions.q: If the density of a solid is ρ(x,y,z), its mass is obtained from
questions.explanation: Mass is the volume integral of density over the solid.

questions.q: To find the volume of a solid using a triple integral, the integrand is generally
questions.explanation: Volume is V = ∭_V 1 dV.

questions.q: The area of a planar region R can be obtained using a double integral as
questions.explanation: Integrating 1 over the region sums its differential area elements.

questions.q: When a region is symmetric about the y-axis and f(x,y) is odd in x, the double integral over the region is
questions.explanation: Opposite points contribute equal and opposite values for an odd integrand over a symmetric region.

questions.q: For the transformation x=u+v, y=u−v, the absolute Jacobian |∂(x,y)/∂(u,v)| is
questions.explanation: The determinant is (1)(−1)−(1)(1)=−2, so its absolute value is 2.

questions.q: A correct change of variables in a multiple integral requires changing
options: the variables, region and Jacobian consistently
questions.answer: the variables, region and Jacobian consistently
questions.explanation: The transformation must be applied to the integrand, differential element and limits/region.

questions.q: The double integral ∫₀²∫₀¹ 1 dy dx gives the area of a
questions.explanation: The limits describe 0≤x≤2 and 0≤y≤1, giving area 2.

questions.q: For a region described by y between g₁(x) and g₂(x), the inner integral with respect to y normally has limits
questions.explanation: For vertical strips, y varies from the lower curve to the upper curve.

questions.q: The region 0≤θ≤2π in polar coordinates represents
questions.explanation: An angular change of 2π covers the complete circle around the origin.

questions.q: For a cylinder x²+y²≤a² with 0≤z≤h, cylindrical coordinates are advantageous because
options: the radial and angular limits describe the circular cross-section naturally
questions.answer: the radial and angular limits describe the circular cross-section naturally
questions.explanation: The circular boundary becomes r≤a, simplifying the multiple integral.

questions.q: If a coordinate transformation has Jacobian zero at a point, the transformation is locally
questions.explanation: A zero Jacobian indicates local degeneracy and prevents a regular local change of variables at that point.

questions.q: The main reason for selecting polar, cylindrical or spherical coordinates is to
options: match the geometry and simplify the integral
questions.answer: match the geometry and simplify the integral
questions.explanation: Coordinate systems are chosen to represent the region and integrand more naturally, reducing calculation effort.
